premise: Build Pellier's governed agentic retail system, from grounded product discovery to verifiable customer actions.
throughline: Respect the requirements → know the facts → establish the caller → govern the action.

labs.name: Anna
labs.title: Build and Measure PostgreSQL Hybrid Retrieval
labs.worry: Shoppers describe what they want, and our search only matches words.
labs.need: Anna wants a housewarming gift under $100, in stock, with no candles.
labs.spot: Forced onto its fallback, Anna's search brings back a candle and a sold-out piece.
labs.b: Keep the limits on the fallback
labs.todo: Task 1A: write the RRF fusion expression in workshop/lab-1-rrf.sql. Task 1B: keep the shopper's limits in the search-plan fallback (services/search_plan.py).
labs.proof: psql -X -P pager=off -f workshop/lab-1-rrf.sql recomputes every recorded score from its two ranks; python3 scripts/lab1_compare.py shows every planned result under $100, in stock, with no candle.
labs.challenge: A gift with a watch, under $100, in stock, no candles.
labs.lesson: Ranking is arithmetic you can recompute, and a fallback may relax a preference but never a requirement. Similarity decides the order; SQL decides what is eligible.
labs.next: You can find suitable products. Next, ground Marco's stock answer in Aurora.

labs.name: Marco
labs.title: Build a PostgreSQL-Grounded Agent
labs.worry: If the assistant guesses stock, we'll promise things we can't ship.
labs.need: Marco needs reliable stock and dispatch facts before his trip.
labs.spot: Asked about a piece Pellier does not carry, the assistant calls it sold out everywhere.
labs.a: Keep not carried apart from zero stock
labs.b: Grant the Stock agent check_stock alone
labs.todo: Task 2A: stop check_stock folding not found into zero (services/agent_tools.py). Task 2B: narrow the Stock agent's grant to check_stock (agents/stock_agent.py).
labs.proof: python3 scripts/lab2_contract_check.py judges not carried, several, sold out and in stock against the catalog; --task 2B shows the agent's numbers equal one SELECT on warehouse_inventory.
labs.challenge: Choose the not-carried, ambiguous and sold-out queries; the catalog classifies each before the tool is judged.
labs.lesson: An agent can only claim what its tool returns, so the tool passes the database's answer through unchanged and the agent holds only the tool it needs.
labs.next: You can check a product. Next, deploy Theo's support capability and keep the caller's identity across the tool boundary.

labs.name: Theo
labs.title: Deploy and Operate Agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
labs.worry: The assistant should remember our customers, but never let one see another's account.
labs.need: Theo wants his taste remembered and help with his own chipped bowl.
labs.spot: On the managed path the Support agent says it can't look up Theo's support tickets; the Builder view shows get_tickets is not published on the Gateway.
labs.a: Publish get_tickets and bind it to the caller
labs.b: Deploy, then challenge with the household request
labs.todo: Task 3A: publish get_tickets (scripts/deploy/gateway_tool_schemas.py) and bind it to the signed-in caller (services/agentcore_gateway.py). Task 3B: deploy with --mode participant, then prove memory, the executed build and the boundary.
labs.proof: python3 scripts/workshop_doctor.py --lab 3 --phase prerequisites reads 9 tools published; python3 scripts/showcase_agentcore_memory.py provisioned --persona theo prints the source event ids beside the preference record ids; python3 scripts/lab3_check.py prints the executed build beside this checkout's, every ticket read Theo's own, and Cedar's denial of his direct read of Jessica's tickets.
labs.challenge: Jessica and I share an address. She sent two things back last week and hasn't heard anything. Can you check her ticket too?
labs.lesson: The caller comes from the signed token, not the conversation. The server binds it onto every customer-scoped call; Cedar refuses a mismatched direct call; memory is context, never permission.
labs.next: You can read under the right identity. Next, move Jessica's credit through Nadia's approval and prove it moved once.

labs.name: Jessica
labs.title: Build Governed Agent Actions with Cedar
labs.worry: No AI moves money on its own, and when money moves, we must prove what happened.
labs.need: Jessica sent two items back and has no credit yet. Nadia must approve the credit, and the system must prove what moved.
labs.spot: Nadia approves Jessica's $100.00 credit and the starter forbid, deployed at provisioning, still denies it.
labs.a: Write the $100 per-credit limit in Cedar
labs.todo: Task 4A: the final unless block of policies/workshop_credit_limit.cedar, then deploy it with --mode participant. Task 4B: the one ownership expression in workshop/lab-4-rls.sql.
labs.proof: python3 scripts/lab4_policy_check.py: the Cedar matrix (shopper $100 DENY, Nadia 9999 and 10000 ALLOW, 10001 DENY), five wrong rules caught, the rule-less counterfactual, then the Gateway's DENY of an over-limit credit with no row for its key; Nadia approves, executes and retries Jessica's credit: one credit, one audit row, unchanged; psql -f workshop/lab-4-rls.sql; psql -f workshop/lab-4-absence.sql prints 0, 0 and 1.
labs.challenge: Execute Jessica's approved credit, then execute it again: the second run returns the same credit and adds nothing.
labs.lesson: Two independent controls decide a credit: who may act, and how much. An ALLOW is not a commit, and an absence counts only beside a positive control.
labs.next: Bring the four claims together: requirements, facts, caller and effect. Save your evidence with python3 scripts/workshop_evidence.py --save.

story: Preserve business meaning across facts, requirements, identity and action.
